title: Design System: Jasmine Vir · Electrical Engineer

display.purpose: The name on the cover only, uppercase, spanned by a dimension line.

headline.purpose: Sheet titles with the double drawing-title underline.

title.purpose: Revision roles; the cover role line and detail titles run a step smaller.

title-sm.purpose: Legend entries, title-block project line, index name, legend and end-of-set titles.

lead.purpose: Cover tagline within 40ch; first general note and contact lead are close variants.

body.purpose: Reading text with tabular numerals; notes 1.0625rem within 64ch, summaries within 52ch.

label.purpose: Uppercase field labels in drafting objects and forms, and the text of the top-right controls.

mono.purpose: Uppercase sheet numbers, codes, dates, dimensions, plotter status.

hand.purpose: Redline and checker markup notes, rotated -2 to -3deg.

shadows.name: drawer-lift
shadows.purpose: Sheet-index drawer only; backdrop rgb(4 18 40 / 0.35) on the blueprint, rgb(15 58 114 / 0.18) on the whiteprint.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: State changes (0.2-0.45s), breaker blades (0.5-0.6s), drawer entry, switch knob, cover text rise.

motion.name: ease-plot
motion.purpose: Plotter stroke draws (1.4-1.6s), loader exposure wipe (0.9s), print wipe (0.7s), dimension line reveal.

motion.name: plot
motion.purpose: How every drawing enters; labels fade in after ~0.9s.

motion.name: print-wipe
motion.purpose: Switching prints wipes the new sheet down over the old one; skipped under reduced motion.

motion.name: drawer
motion.value: opacity 0.3s + translate 24px -> 0 over 0.35s ease-out, @starting-style, display/overlay allow-discrete

motion.name: state
motion.purpose: Button, link, control, and index hover/current transitions.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Loader hidden, smooth scroll off, print wipe skipped, drawings and breakers shown in final state.

components.name: Breaker
components.description: Sheet breaker on the bus; blade closes and takes the highlighter line when its sheet is live.

narrative.overview:
The whole site is one electrical drawing set, issued in two print processes from the same originals. The default is a blueprint (cyanotype): Prussian-blue paper with a mottled exposure and darkened edges, pale diazo-white linework and lettering. The alternate is a whiteprint (diazo): pale paper with Prussian linework, an amber highlighter line, and a darker redline. Every surface is a drafting object with a real job on a real sheet: a fixed border with zone letters and numbers, a title block, a sheet index, numbered general notes, a symbol legend, a revision table, detail bubbles, and an RFI form. Nothing is a card, and nothing is rounded except what a draftsman would draw with a circle template.

Density is that of a working sheet: generous margins around content, fine and heavy rules doing all structural work, drafted condensed capitals for every heading, set at a moderate scale so the sheet reads as a drawing rather than a poster. A single one-line power diagram is the system's spine: the cover's switchboard feeds a bus down the left margin, each sheet hangs off it through a breaker, and scrolling energizes it with the highlighter. Motion behaves like a plotter and a print machine: strokes draw on, and switching prints wipes the new sheet down over the old one.

Color is spent like ink on a markup set. Paper and line carry everything; the highlighter means energized, checked, current, or focused; the redline means placeholder, error, or the one primary action. Those meanings are fixed in both prints. A small control block at the top right (JV monogram, print switch, index button) is the only chrome; the sheet index lives in a drawer opened on demand.
keyCharacteristics: Two prints, one system: every color is a custom property, redefined as a whole set under the whiteprint theme; components never hard-code a color.
Paper ground with a shared texture layer (vignette, exposure mottle, paper fibre) on every opaque surface, recut for each print.
Linework hierarchy instead of elevation: 1px fine rules, 1.5px heavy rules, double rules under drawing titles.
Barlow Condensed drafted capitals for headings, Barlow for reading, Red Hat Mono for numbers and codes, Kalam for handwritten markup.
Square corners everywhere; circles only as drafting symbols.
Authored SVG drawings (one-line, breakers, legend symbols, detail drawings, the monogram) with round-capped strokes so every stroke can plot.
Placeholder content is visibly redlined until replaced.

rules.name: The Two Pens Rule
rules.body: Only two colors exist beyond paper and line. Highlighter means energized, checked, current, or focused; red means placeholder, error, or primary action. Never use either decoratively, and never swap their jobs, in either print.

rules.name: The Two Prints Rule
rules.body: Both themes are the same drawing set. A new color is added as a custom property in both the blueprint `:root` and the whiteprint override, never as a literal in a component; role names stay the same across prints and only values change.

rules.name: The One Redline Action Rule
rules.body: A surface layer carries at most one filled redline button. On the sheet that is the cover's "Issue an RFI"; every other action there is a ghost outline. The sheet-index drawer is its own overlay layer, so its RFI button is primary.

rules.name: The Line Is Not Text Rule
rules.body: Fine Rule and Hairline are line weights, not text colors. Any readable text uses Line or Tinted Line.

rules.name: The Drafted Capitals Rule
rules.body: Every heading and action button is Barlow Condensed 600, uppercase, lightly tracked. Utility controls (print switch, index toggle) are tracked Barlow label caps. Reading text is never set in capitals.

rules.name: The Mono Is For Numbers Rule
rules.body: Red Hat Mono carries sheet numbers, codes, dates, dimensions, and plotter status, never sentences or field labels. Labels are tracked Barlow caps.

rules.name: The Handwriting Is Markup Rule
rules.body: Kalam appears only as a pen annotation in Redline or Highlighter Line (or Tinted Line for "Fed from" notes), slightly rotated, never as a heading or body.

rules.name: The Hang It On The Bus Rule
rules.body: Every sheet header connects to the left-margin bus through its breaker; new sections join the circuit rather than float free of it.

rules.name: The Line Weight Is Depth Rule
rules.body: Hierarchy between surfaces is expressed by 1px fine versus 1.5px heavy rules and by double title rules, never by shadows. The only shadow belongs to the drawer, which genuinely overlays the sheet.

rules.name: The Circle Template Rule
rules.body: A circle is a symbol, never a softened corner. If it is not a node, pad, terminal, bubble, or component symbol, it is square.

dos: Do build every new surface as a drafting object (sheet, schedule, detail, note, table) on Paper with Line linework, and check it in both prints.
Do add every new color as a custom property in both the blueprint `:root` and the `:root[data-theme="light"]` override.

Do keep the highlighter for energized, checked, current, and focus states (Highlighter Line for strokes and text, Checker's Highlighter for fills), and red for placeholders, errors, and the single primary action.
Do set every heading in Barlow Condensed 600 uppercase with the double drawing-title underline on sheet and detail titles.
Do separate and frame with 1px Fine Rule / Hairline and 1.5px Heavy Rule lines.
Do author drawings as inline SVG with `pathLength=1` strokes, 1.5px round-capped, so they can plot on entry with the plot curve (cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.2, 1)).
Do keep chrome inside the top-right control block and put navigation in the drawer rather than docking new fixed panels.
Do show content in its final state without JavaScript and under reduced motion.
donts: Don't hard-code a color literal in a component; it will be wrong in the other print.
Don't round corners on containers, buttons, controls, or inputs; circles are drafting symbols only.
Don't add shadows to express hierarchy; only the overlaying drawer gets a shadow.
Don't put a second filled redline button on the same surface layer.
Don't set readable text in Fine Rule or Hairline; they are line weights.
Don't use Red Hat Mono for sentences or field labels, or Kalam for anything but pen markup.
Don't fade or slide drawings in; they plot.
